title: KCV–AEAD Compatibility Without a Separate KDF
summary: The generic construction requires a collision-resistant PRF KDF to separate the AEAD key; identifying and analyzing secure KCV–AEAD pairs that reuse the original key remains open.

formal_statement.body: A generic key-check-value construction derives an independent authenticated-encryption-with-associated-data (AEAD) key through a separate key-derivation function (KDF), which must be a collision-resistant pseudorandom function and therefore adds overhead. This overhead may be unnecessary when the key identifier is never used in the AEAD scheme's internal computation. Identify concrete pairs of key-check-value functions and AEAD schemes that can securely share the original key without a separate KDF, and provide a security analysis establishing their compatibility.

scope.domain: Shared-key composition of key-check-value functions with authenticated-encryption-with-associated-data schemes.
assumptions: The key identifier is never used in the AEAD scheme's internal computation.
parameters: Choice of key-check-value function and AEAD scheme—the concrete pair evaluated for shared-key compatibility
scope.unresolved_remainder: Identify concrete compatible pairs that can securely share the original key without a separate KDF and establish their compatibility through security analysis.

progress.summary: The paper explains that its generic approach derives an independent AEAD key using a collision-resistant PRF KDF, adding potentially avoidable overhead. It explicitly leaves pair-specific analysis without a separate KDF as an open problem.
citation_labels: Julia Len et al., Authenticated Encryption with Key Identification
